name: International Cooperation & Global Frameworks for DRR

notes.heading: International Cooperation in Disaster Management
points: Disasters often transcend national boundaries and require global cooperation
Countries share knowledge, technology, and resources for disaster risk reduction (DRR)
International cooperation helps in early warning systems and emergency response
Developed countries support developing countries through funding and capacity building
Global institutions coordinate disaster preparedness and recovery efforts

notes.heading: Need for International Cooperation
points: Increasing frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters
Transboundary nature of disasters like tsunamis and cyclones
Resource and technology gaps in developing countries
Need for coordinated early warning systems
Global climate change impacts all nations collectively

notes.heading: United Nations and Disaster Risk Reduction
points: United Nations plays a central role in global disaster management
UNDRR (United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction) coordinates DRR efforts
Focus on reducing disaster losses globally
Promotes international frameworks and agreements
Encourages resilience-building in member countries

notes.heading: Hyogo Framework for Action (2005–2015)
points: First major global framework for disaster risk reduction
Adopted in Kobe, Japan in 2005
Aim: Build resilience of nations and communities to disasters
Focused on risk identification, preparedness, and capacity building
Laid foundation for modern DRR strategies

notes.heading: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)
points: Adopted in Sendai, Japan in 2015
Successor to Hyogo Framework
Focus on reducing disaster risk rather than managing disasters
Four priorities: understanding risk, strengthening governance, investing in DRR, enhancing preparedness
Aims to reduce disaster mortality, affected people, and economic losses

notes.heading: Key Features of Sendai Framework
points: People-centered approach to disaster risk reduction
Emphasis on risk-informed development planning
Strong focus on early warning systems
Integration of climate change adaptation and DRR
Encourages international cooperation and technology sharing

notes.heading: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and DRR
points: DRR is integrated into SDGs, especially Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)
Focus on making cities inclusive, safe, and resilient
Link between poverty reduction and disaster resilience
Climate action (Goal 13) directly connected with DRR
Promotes sustainable and risk-informed development

notes.heading: Other Global Initiatives
points: UN Climate Change Framework (UNFCCC) – addresses climate-related disasters
Paris Agreement – focuses on climate change mitigation and adaptation
International Strategy for Disaster Reduction (ISDR)
World Bank funding for disaster resilience projects
Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement – humanitarian response

notes.heading: Current Developments in Disaster Management
points: Increased focus on climate-resilient infrastructure
Use of satellite technology and AI for early warning systems
Community-based disaster risk reduction programs
Strengthening of global early warning systems (UN initiatives)
Integration of digital technology in disaster response

name: International Partnerships, India’s Leadership & Bilateral Cooperation

notes.heading: Partnerships with International Agencies – Overview
points: India actively collaborates with international organizations for disaster risk reduction and response
These partnerships focus on capacity building, technology transfer, and early warning systems
Global cooperation helps India manage large-scale disasters more effectively
Coordination occurs through UN bodies, regional platforms, and financial institutions
Emphasis is on building resilience and sharing best practices

notes.heading: Major International Agencies Involved
points: UNDRR (United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction) – global DRR coordination
UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) – capacity building and governance support
UNOCHA (UN Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs) – emergency response coordination
World Bank – funding disaster resilience and recovery projects
Asian Development Bank (ADB) – infrastructure and disaster risk financing
International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement – humanitarian relief operations

notes.heading: Areas of Cooperation with International Agencies
points: Early warning systems for cyclones, floods, and tsunamis
Climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies
Training of disaster response teams
Development of resilient infrastructure
Disaster risk financing and insurance mechanisms

notes.heading: India’s Leadership Initiatives in Disaster Management
points: India plays a proactive role in global disaster risk reduction platforms
Initiated the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)
Promotes South-South cooperation in disaster management
Hosts training programs for neighboring countries
Provides rapid humanitarian assistance during regional disasters

notes.heading: Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)
points: Launched by India in 2019
A global partnership of countries and organizations
Focuses on making infrastructure resilient to climate and disaster risks
Works on knowledge sharing, technical support, and capacity building
Supports sustainable development goals through resilient infrastructure

notes.heading: India’s Role in Regional Cooperation
points: Active member of SAARC Disaster Management Centre initiatives
Cooperation with BIMSTEC for disaster preparedness
Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) focuses on maritime disaster response
India provides cyclone warnings to neighboring countries
Assistance during earthquakes, floods, and tsunamis in the region

notes.heading: Bilateral Agreements with Countries
points: India signs MoUs for disaster management cooperation with various countries
Focus on knowledge exchange and joint training programs
Assistance in emergency response and relief operations
Technology sharing in satellite-based monitoring and forecasting
Mutual support during large-scale disasters

notes.heading: Examples of Bilateral Cooperation
points: India–Japan cooperation in earthquake and tsunami preparedness
India–USA collaboration on climate resilience and disaster response
India–Australia cooperation on cyclone forecasting and maritime safety
India–France partnership on climate and environmental risk reduction
India–Nepal and India–Bhutan cooperation in Himalayan disaster management

notes.heading: Significance of International Partnerships
points: Improves disaster preparedness and response capacity
Enhances access to advanced technology and forecasting systems
Strengthens regional and global coordination
Reduces loss of lives and economic damage
Supports sustainable and resilient development
